sources.entry: code-server - VS Code in the browser, hosted on a remote server. MIT Nodejs/Docker
Code-Server | Run VS Code on any machine anywhere

summary.one_liner: code-server runs VS Code on a remote machine and lets you access it through a web browser.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes code-server as a way to run VS Code on any machine and access it in the browser. It positions the setup as a consistent development environment reachable from any device, with intensive tasks such as compiling, testing, and downloads running on the server rather than the client. It lists five ways to get started: an install script (which uses the system package manager where possible), manual installation, deploying to a team with coder/coder, one-click cloud deployment buttons and guides, and the devcontainers feature. The install script has a --dry-run preview option. The stated minimum requirement is a Linux machine with WebSockets enabled, 1 GB RAM, and 2 vCPUs. The README points to separate docs for FAQs, setup and configuration, and contributing.
use_cases: run VS Code in a browser
develop on a remote cloud server
offload compiles and tests to a server
code from a tablet or laptop on the go
deploy a shared browser IDE for a team
notable: Runs the full VS Code editor in the browser on a self-managed server
Install script with a --dry-run preview and system package manager support
Devcontainers integration for projects already using devcontainers
Pairs with coder/coder for team-wide deployments
caveats: Requires a Linux machine with WebSockets enabled (minimum 1 GB RAM, 2 vCPUs)
Team management across infrastructure is handled by a separate project, coder/coder
